beginner.summary: For developers, system administrators and security engineers who are new to Keycloak and need to add single sign-on to applications. Covers the Quarkus distribution in development mode, the admin console and master realm, realms, users, groups and roles, OIDC clients and the authorization code flow with PKCE, tokens, client scopes and mappers, securing a single-page app and an API, service accounts, self-service and email, password policies, brute force detection, TOTP, sessions and logout, events, and realm export and import, ending with an SSO capstone for two applications.
prerequisites: Understands HTTP, URLs, cookies and redirects and can use curl and browser developer tools
Can run containers with Docker or Podman and edit files from a terminal
Has built or deployed a simple web application or API in any language
outcomes: Run Keycloak locally and manage realms, users, groups and roles in the admin console
Register OIDC clients and run the authorization code flow with PKCE, client credentials and token introspection
Secure a single-page app and a backend API with Keycloak tokens, scopes and role checks
Apply password policies, brute force detection, OTP, session limits and event auditing to a realm
